messages:
nina: hit an unsettling race during a prefix handoff spike. concurrent write + delete interleaved across old/new owner and compaction produced a stale-visible state.

alex: can you share the condensed trace? was the write forwarded or applied locally?

nina: logs: 
```
handoff start id=hf-9 epoch=5 prefix=usr:xyz
old_owner applied del k=usr:xyz:12 epoch=5
concurrent write seq=777 routed to old_owner -> applied locally epoch=4
new_owner later applied same write seq=777 epoch=4
compaction: tombstone epoch=5 vs write epoch=4 -> ordering produced visible write after delete
```
old owner didn't forward, so duplicate apply + epoch tagging caused paradox.

maria: short-term fix: make old owner enter TRANSFERRING state and synchronously forward writes to new owner for a bounded window. keep reads local.

sam: forwarding is transparent but adds latency. maybe gateways should proactively route to new_owner when they see a TRANSFERRING hint. first-forward can act as a hint.

tyler: also need deterministic conflict rule: compare (migration_epoch, op_seq, op_uuid). tombstone wins if migration_epoch > write.migration_epoch or seq higher. encode tombstone_epoch in prefix metadata.

alex: implementation sketch for spike: 1) old flips metadata -> TRANSFERRING(epoch). 2) any write to old -> replicate_and_ack(new_owner) and append op_id to local migration_journal. 3) new persists op before ack. 4) coordinator finalizes by CAS after drain. 5) gateways subscribe to migration hints for sticky routing.

maria: add metrics: migration_forward_count, migration_forward_p99, migration_journal_len, tombstone_epoch_mismatch_count.

ops-bot: spike-branch-created: CI queued.

sam: one more: crash scenario: if old dies mid-drain, coordinator must fetch migration_journal (or request replays) and ensure pending ops delivered to new before finalizing. add replay API.

nina: good. I'll write the RFC PR with ordering rules + dedupe via op_id. we'll canary on ~5 hot prefixes and monitor p99.

alex: +1. closing thread, will file tickets and attach logs.
